A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fish-Vista, using the same museum sources and three principal tasks. All 26 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including appendices, tables, figures, and equations, support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent identifying the substantive changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, trait-identification, and segmentation experiments, including imbalance comparisons, attention-map evaluation, and supplementary segmentation analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original results across the three tasks, additional foundation-model comparisons, and quantitative validation of fish detection and background removal.

M1.justification: The core curation pipeline remains. The stated Grounding DINO prompt changes from 'complete fish' to 'fish'. V2 also introduces a limited procedural extension for zero-shot trait segmentation: Molmo generates points for SAM-v2, followed by explicit mask-overlap resolution (Appendix G.3.1). Expanded descriptions of existing filtering alone do not establish further method changes.

E1.justification: Fish-Vista expands from 1,888 to 4,154 species, substantially broadening evaluated taxonomic coverage. Classification expands from 419 species to 1,758, including an ultra-rare population; v2 Figure 3 and Appendix F.1 give 1,758, although the main text inconsistently says 1,785. Segmentation expands from approximately 1,200 to 3,131 species. The three primary tasks and museum-image domain remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds INTR and linear-probe comparisons using CLIP, BioCLIP, and DINOv2; segmentation adds Mask2Former, YOLOv8, and Molmo+SAM. SegFormer is removed. The imbalance comparison replaces hard balancing, inverse-frequency weighting, and M2m with effective-sample class-balanced weighting and its focal-loss combination. ResNet-18 and Swin-B-1k disappear from classification comparisons, although they remain in identification.

E3.justification: Classification eligibility changes from at least 20 to 4 images per species, with reduced minimum test/validation allocations. Identification replaces evaluation on all FV-1200 images with a 1,281-image manual set explicitly excluding training species. Segmentation changes from reported random splitting to trait-stratified splitting, and from MMSegmentation with 1,000 training epochs to SMP/Adam with up to 100 epochs, early stopping, and revised augmentation.

E4.justification: V2 adds qualitative pipeline audits and quantitative Grounding DINO/SAM validation on 311 bounding-box and 492 segmentation examples. It expands segmentation confusion analysis from one to five models and revises imbalance experiments. Conversely, v1's individual adipose/barbel training experiments, area-versus-IoU analysis, supplementary Swin imbalance comparison, and segmentation pretraining comparisons are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports benchmark run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. The reported normalization statistics concern preprocessing, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Classification and segmentation results are extensively replaced under changed datasets and settings; MaxViT-T classification F1 changes from 85.9% to 57.8%, which is not a comparable-setting performance decline. Even retained identification splits have changed values: VGG-19 in-species mAP changes from 86.3% to 87.06% (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 7). New comparator results and pipeline-validation scores are also added.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix G.1.3 adds an explicit effective-sample weighting definition in place of v1's inverse-frequency rule. Its displayed equation, w_k=(1-beta^N_k)/(1-beta), increases with class size and conflicts with the accompanying inverse-weighting description. This is a limited mathematical addition; neither version develops theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a curated fish dataset supporting classification, trait identification, and segmentation. V2 adds explicit claims of being the first organismal image dataset designed for visual-trait analysis and having a fully reproducible pipeline, while emphasizing computer-vision research challenges more directly.

C2.justification: The principal interpretations concerning unseen-species generalization and small, rare traits remain. V2 explicitly qualifies species-level labels when traits are occluded and discusses segmentation annotation scarcity as a limitation. It also interprets foundation-model results as promising for trait localization and replaces universal segmentation-failure language with model-dependent difficulties.

D1.justification: V2 adds filtering fields and thresholds, SAM configuration, zero-shot prompt ensembling, and detailed Molmo/SAM model and inference settings. However, v1 Appendix A provides public HuggingFace download instructions and a public code repository; v2 Appendices A-B instead describe anonymous code, metadata, and sample images, with the complete image release and dataset card deferred. This materially changes documented reproducibility and access.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including BioSCAN-5M and newly evaluated methods, and more explicitly distinguishes FishNet's functional traits from image-localizable visual traits. The underlying positioning against classification-focused biodiversity datasets remains. FishNet and BioCLIP were already discussed in v1.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, dataset exposition, and results narrative are extensively rewritten around computer-vision challenges. Task descriptions are reorganized, numerical dataset names become task-based names, and new motivation and insights passages structure the argument. The appendices are substantially reorganized into release, processing, dataset, implementation, and results sections.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, redesigns the task overview, consolidates dataset statistics into Figure 3, and adds processing examples. Classification results are redistributed between the main text and appendix, the segmentation table is restructured, and the single confusion matrix becomes a five-model panel. Several older diagnostic plots disappear.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through broader species coverage, direct pipeline validation, and expanded comparisons. However, it replaces v1's public download instructions with partial anonymous materials and a promised full release, removes useful diagnostics, and introduces an internally inconsistent class-weight equation. These substantial empirical gains coexist with reproducibility and reporting regressions, preventing a reliable net quality judgment from the PDFs.
